answer: Sybil clones win by volume: a script templates a thousand answers, flooding the epoch. Use a distinctiveness gate: each answer is scored by compression distance against all others; duplicates are rejected before they earn. A farm's clones all compress to the same codebook, forcing the operator to pay human writers per clone—$8 each, $8,000 per thousand clones—to clear the gate. Each clone needs its own bonded key and a fresh answer bond, so the farm pays twice. Ivory is carved one piece at a time; a meadow holds distinct flowers; a tundra script farm grows nothing but copies.
